paragraphs.text: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 is an autosomal recessive syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta. Its main features are bone fragility with multiple fractures, which can begin before birth, and severely disturbed ossification of the skull. Craniofacial malformations include macrocephaly, frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia and micrognathia, and patients can also have short stature (Garbes et al., 2015; Takeyari et al., 2018).

checks.explanation: Syndromic OI is stated; autosomal recessive is only implied by compound heterozygosity, not stated.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) reported 3 affected individuals from 2 families with a similar skeletal phenotype. One was a 7-year-old boy and the other 2 were fetuses from 1 family, initially suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta. All 3 had severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures that began before birth. The boy had short stature and craniofacial malformations including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing, and down-slanting palpebral fissures. Garbes et al. (2015) noted that cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia (CLSD) has a largely overlapping craniofacial phenotype but lacks generalized bone fragility, and that cataracts were present in the original CLSD family.

paragraphs.text: Zhang et al. (2017) reported 2 Chinese families with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta. The proband in family 1 was a 23-year-old man with recurrent fractures and dentinogenesis imperfecta. His anterior fontanel had not closed, and he showed facial dysmorphism. Three-dimensional computed tomography of the cranium showed skull deformities with a broad ossification defect in the frontoapical area, a widened sagittal suture, and Wormian bones. The proband in family 2 was a 7-year-old boy who also had recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta and an unclosed anterior fontanel, but no obvious facial dysmorphism.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) used whole-exome sequencing to study 3 individuals from 2 families with a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta. They identified 3 mutant alleles of the SEC24D gene: a truncating c.613C-T mutation (gln205-to-ter; Q205X); a c.3044C-T missense mutation (ser1015-to-phe; S1015F), located in a cargo-binding pocket; and a c.2933A-C missense mutation (gln978-to-pro; Q978P), located in the gelsolin-like domain. Each affected individual was compound heterozygous for 2 of these alleles. The c.3044C-T mutation lay on a 14-Mb founder haplotype shared by all 3 individuals.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) used electron and immunofluorescence microscopy to examine skin fibroblasts from an affected boy. The cells showed inefficient export of procollagen from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and dilated ER tubules. This reproduced the cellular phenotype of cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia caused by SEC23A mutations. The authors stated that the cellular and morphologic phenotypes were concordant with those of Sec24d-deficient medaka (vbi) and zebrafish (bulldog) mutants.
